summarize_events.description: The reliability report in one step: how many AWS events there were over a period, how many of each severity, how long they ran in total, which was the longest, and which services and regions had the most. Written for the monthly review that would otherwise mean counting a list by hand. Narrow to the regions and the service you run on.

mock_response.summary: The AWS Health Dashboard recorded 4 events active between 2026-07-01 and 2026-09-14: 1 service disruption, 1 service degradation and 2 informational events, most often in US East (N. Virginia).

summarize_events.name: summarize_events

parameters.description: The first day to include, counted in, as a whole UTC day. Leave it empty for everything the dashboard still holds. An event that began before this date and was still running on it is included, because it was part of that day. The dashboard publishes only the recent past, so the result also reports the earliest date it actually covers: a date before that is unanswerable rather than quiet.
parameters.name: start_date

parameters.description: The last day to include, counted in, as a whole UTC day. Leave it empty to run up to now. It must be on or after the start date.
parameters.name: end_date

parameters.description: Narrow the answer to the AWS regions you actually run in. Pick as many as you like, or leave it empty for everywhere. A multi-region event counts for every region it names, not just the one AWS filed it under, so a filter on eu-west-1 still catches an event AWS opened against us-east-1 that reached Ireland. 'Global' covers the services that are not regional at all, such as CloudFront, Route 53, Billing and the console.
parameters.name: regions

parameters.description: Only events touching this AWS service. Pick one, or type a name - 's3', 'EC2' and 'Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud' all find the right one. Leave it empty for every service. A big multi-service event counts for every service it names, not only the one in its headline.
parameters.name: service

description: Watch the public AWS Health Dashboard from a workflow. Ask whether AWS is having problems right now, whether one service or one region is affected, and what every open event is. Pull an event's full update timeline for a postmortem, list what happened over a date range, and summarize a period for a reliability report. Filter by the regions you actually run in, so an outage on the other side of the world stays quiet, and by severity, so a routine notice does not page anyone. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No AWS account, credentials or support plan required.
